rationale: Both use a correct flood fill seeded from the player's starting edge, with the same six-neighbour offsets, and both are well documented. A's design is elegant: one closure takes start-edge and end-edge predicates, and the offsets are a package-level table. However, it assumes every row has the width of lines[0] and silently accepts any character. B is more robust beyond the tests. It validates the board characters and uses the error return the signature provides. It also sizes each visited row and checks bounds per line, so ragged input cannot cause an out-of-range panic. B also splits the work into top-level connects and neighbors functions, which are easy to test and read. Its horizontal boolean flag and the compound edge expressions are a bit less elegant than A's predicates, but B's extra safety and clear structure give it the edge.
